extracted.intended_audience: EPA officials and staff, agency lawyers, federal practitioners, and members of the public seeking authoritative information on EPA organization and office responsibilities
extracted.subtask_description: Codified statements defining the Environmental Protection Agency's creation, purpose, organizational structure (Headquarters and Regional Offices), the functions and duties of specific Headquarters offices and suboffices, regional boundaries, and authorities under federal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creation and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Reorganization Plan 3 of 1970 established the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) in the Executive branch as an independent Agency, effective December 2, 1970.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency permits coordinated and effective governmental action to assure the protection of the environment by abating and controlling pollution on a systematic basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EPA coordinates research, monitoring, standard setting, and enforcement activities; supports research and antipollution activities by State and local governments, private and public groups, individuals, and educational institutions; and reinforces efforts among other Federal agencies regarding environmental impacts of their operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and general information (Headquarters and Regional Offices)
rubrics_metrics.description: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency's basic organization consists of Headquarters and 10 Regional Offices. EPA Headquarters in Washington, DC maintains overall planning, coordination and control of EPA programs. Regional Administrators head the Regional Offices and are responsible directly to the Administrator for the execution of the Agency's programs within the boundaries of their Regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directives System availability
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA's Directives System contains definitive statements of EPA's organization, policies, procedures, assignments of responsibility, and delegations of authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies are available for public inspection and copying at the Management and Organization Division, 1200 Pennsylvania Ave., NW., Washington, DC 20460; information can be obtained from the Office of Public Affairs at all Regional Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA conducts procurement pursuant to the Federal Property and Administrative Services Act, the Federal Procurement Regulations, and implementing EPA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location of principal offices and regional coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Headquarters is in Washington, DC. The addresses of the EPA Regional Offices and the States/territories they serve are listed (Regions I–X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Region lists physical address and the States/territories served (e.g., Region I: Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, Rhode Island, and Vermont; Region IX includes certain territories and specified U.S. Government activities in freely associated states).

rubrics_metrics.name: Headquarters composition
rubrics_metrics.description: EPA Headquarters is comprised of: the Office of the Administrator; two Associate Administrators and four staff offices; the Office of Inspector General; the Office of General Counsel; and nine operational offices, each headed by an Assistant Administrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These components advise the Administrator on cross-cutting Agency and regional issues and carry out major environmental and administrative programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and responsibilities of the Administrator and Deputy Administrator
rubrics_metrics.description: The Environmental Protection Agency is headed by an Administrator who is appointed by the President, by and with the consent of the Senate. The Administrator is responsible to the President for providing overall supervision to the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Deputy Administrator, also appointed by the President with Senate consent, assists the Administrator in discharge of duties and serves as Acting Administrator in the Administrator's absence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Administrative Law Judges functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the supervision of the Chief Administrative Law Judge, the Office of Administrative Law Judges is responsible for presiding over and conducting formal hearings, and issuance of initial decisions, if appropriate, in such proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office provides supervision of Administrative Law Judges who operate as a component of the Office in certain Regional Offices and provides the Agency Hearing Clerk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Civil Rights responsibilities and nondiscrimination assurances
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Civil Rights serves as the principal adviser to the Administrator on civil rights programs, develops policies, procedures, and regulations to implement civil rights responsibilities, and provides direction to Regional and field activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office assures: (1) Maximum participation of minority business enterprises under EPA contracts and grants; (2) Equal employment opportunity under Agency service contracts, construction contracts, and grants; (3) Compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act and related acts; (4) Compliance with laws requiring nondiscrimination on account of age and physical handicap; and (5) Services or benefits dispensed under programs receiving Agency financial assistance are nondiscriminatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Science Advisory Board functions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Science Advisory Board provides expert and independent advice to the Administrator on scientific and technical issues facing the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board advises on broad scientific, technical and policy matters; assesses results of specific research; assists in identifying emerging environmental problems; and advises on cohesiveness and currency of the Agency's scientific programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for developing policy and procedures implementing the Agency's small and disadvantaged business utilization responsibilities and providing information and assistance to Agency components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develops programs to maximize utilization of women-owned and minority business enterprises, collaborates with Procurement and Contracts Management Division, recommends assignment of technical advisers to assist Procurement Center Representatives, and represents EPA at hearings and interagency forums on these matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Appeals Board composition, functions, and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The Environmental Appeals Board is a permanent body composed of no more than four Board Members designated by the Administrator. The Board shall decide matters in accordance with applicable statutes and regulations and typically sits in three-Member panels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions include exercising authority delegated to it, providing advice and consultation, making findings of fact and conclusions of law, preparing recommended decisions, or serving as the final decisionmaker. Qualifications: each member must be a graduate of an accredited law school and a member in good standing of a recognized State or DC bar; Board Members shall not be employed by offices directly associated with matters that could come before the Board. Recusal: a Board Member must recuse if previously performed prosecutorial/investigative functions, participated in preparation/presentation of evidence, or was otherwise personally involved in the case. In event of tie vote, matter is referred to the Administrator to break the tie.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of International Activities responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides direction and supervision of Agency international programs and activities, develops policies and procedures for international programs subject to U.S. foreign policy, and assures adequate program, scientific, and legal inputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinates Agency international contacts, serves as point of contact for foreign visitors, negotiates arrangements for international cooperation, maintains liaison with international organizations, approves annual plans for travel abroad and attendance at international events, provides administrative support for executive secretariat activities, and supervises programs wholly within EPA purview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Regional Operations responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports to the Administrator and Deputy Administrator; serves as primary communications link between Headquarters and Regional Administrators and ensures Regional involvement in Agency decision-making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assures Regional participation, assesses impact of Headquarters actions on Regions, acts as ombudsman to resolve Regional problems, coordinates Regional issues and meetings, organizes Regional responses, monitors responsiveness and compliance with established policies, and conducts on-site field visits to resolve Regional and national issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Inspector General duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Assumes overall responsibility for audits and investigations relating to EPA programs and operations and provides leadership and coordination to promote economy, efficiency, and prevent/detect fraud and abuse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informs Administrator, Deputy Administrator, and Congress of serious problems and progress of corrective action; reviews legislation and regulations to assess impacts on administration of EPA programs; recommends policies; conducts or coordinates relations with other government entities on economy and efficiency matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of General Counsel functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as the primary legal adviser to the Administrator and provides legal services to all organizational elements of the Agency with respect to all Agency programs and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides legal opinions, counsel, litigation support, and assists in formulation and administration of Agency policies and programs as legal adviser.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Administration and Resources Management (OARM) functions and components
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Assistant Administrator for Administration and Resources Management, provides services Agencywide for budget, financial management, personnel services, occupational health and safety, administrative services, organization and management analysis and systems development, information management, automated data processing, procurement through contracts and grants, and human resources management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcomponents and responsibilities include: OARM Research Triangle Park (personnel, financial management, procurement, library and IT services); Office of Administration, Cincinnati (personnel, procurement, facilities at Cincinnati and other locations); Office of the Comptroller (budget, fiscal management, accounting systems, allotments, payroll and disbursements); Office of Administration (personnel policies, procurement policies, facilities, security); Office of Information Resources Management (IRM policy, standards, IT acquisition and operations, records management, liaison with OMB and GSA); Office of Human Resources Management (workforce planning, SES policies, training, performance review support, personnel development, workforce analyses). The Assistant Administrator represents EPA in communications with OMB, OPM, GAO, GSA, Treasury, and other agencies on budget and administrative matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Enforcement and Compliance Monitoring responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as the principal adviser to the Administrator in matters concerning enforcement and compliance and provides principal direction and review of civil enforcement activities for air, water, waste, pesticides, toxics, and radiation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manages national criminal enforcement program; ensures coordination of administrative compliance programs and civil/criminal enforcement activities; provides technical expertise for enforcement activities; reviews efforts of Assistant and Regional Administrators to assure a strong and consistent enforcement and compliance monitoring program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of External Affairs functions (Federal Activities and Public Affairs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of External Affairs includes the Office of Federal Activities and Office of Public Affairs, among others, providing liaison, NEPA and EIS oversight, public information, and interagency coordination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office of Federal Activities: national program manager for review of other agency EISs under Section 309 of the Clean Air Act; EPA compliance with NEPA and related laws; Executive policy on American Indian affairs; development/oversight of programs implementing Executive Order 12088 and other requirements concerning compliance by Federal facilities; chairs the Standing Committee on Implementation of EO 12088; administers filing/information system for Federal EISs under agreement with CEQ. Office of Public Affairs: chief spokesperson, principal adviser on public affairs, ensures openness, develops publications and informational materials, maintains clearance systems and procedures, supervises community relations and production of audio-visual materials, reviews interagency agreements and purchase requisitions for public information contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Legislative Analysis responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for legislative drafting and liaison activities relating to Agency programs; acts in capacity of Legislative Counsel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises responsibility for legislative drafting, reports to OMB and congressional committees as required, provides testimony, reviews hearing transcripts, maintains liaison with Office of Congressional Liaison, works closely with program staff in development of legislative initiatives, assists with appropriations and policy coordination, and provides legislative research services via the Legislative Reference Library.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Congressional Liaison functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as principal adviser to the Administrator with respect to congressional activities and is the principal point of congressional contact with the Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains liaison with Congress on Agency activities, assures prompt response to congressional inquiries, coordinates contacts between Comptroller staff and Appropriations Subcommittee staff, and liaises with Regional and field officials as necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Community and Intergovernmental Relations responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as the principal point of contact with public interest groups representing State and local governments, advises on intergovernmental relations, and supports Administrator on intergovernmental issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintains liaison with White House and OMB, identifies intergovernmental issues and solutions, coordinates Administrator involvement with State/local officials, encourages improved State/local methods for EPA program initiatives, tracks legislative initiatives affecting intergovernmental relations, and advises on programs like the President's Environmental Youth Awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Policy, Planning and Evaluation responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistant Administrator serves as principal adviser to the Administrator on Agency policy and planning issues and supervises policy analysis; standards and regulations; and management strategy and evaluation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents the Administrator with Congress, OMB, and other Federal agencies prescribing Government management requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Research and Development (ORD) mission and program elements
rubrics_metrics.description: ORD is responsible for planning, managing, and evaluating a comprehensive research program to develop scientific and technological methods and data needed to understand ecological processes, predict ecosystem impacts, and manage pollutant fate and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program includes: (1) development of organism and ecosystem-level effect data for standards/criteria; (2) development of fate/transport/exposure prediction methods; (3) development/demonstration of control/management methods for adverse impacts; (4) development/demonstration of integrated pest management strategies; (5) development of lab and field-scale screening tests to predict pollutant behavior and impacts; (6) coordination of interagency research on health and environmental impacts of energy production/use; and (7) development/demonstration of methods for restoring degraded ecosystems by means other than source control. ORD includes offices such as Office of Health Research, Office of Health and Environmental Assessment, Office of Exploratory Research, with responsibilities for human health research, criteria and risk assessment, extramural grant management, and related activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Land and Emergency Management responsibilities and statutory programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides Agencywide policy, guidance, and direction for solid and hazardous waste and emergency response programs and has primary responsibility for implementing RCRA, CERCLA (Superfund), the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act, the Oil Pollution Act, Clean Water Act section 311, and the Mercury-Containing and Rechargeable Battery Management Act, among other laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duties include program policy development and evaluation; development of hazardous waste standards and regulations; ensuring compliance with laws; technical support and evaluation of Regional activities; development of guidelines for land disposal of hazardous wastes; response to uncontrolled hazardous waste sites and spills; long-term planning and economic/environmental analyses; and cost-benefit analyses and development of environmental criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Water responsibilities and suboffice functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible for management of EPA's water programs including program policy development, standards development, compliance and permitting activities for drinking water and water programs, technical assistance, demonstration programs, and analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suboffices include: (a) Office of Water Enforcement and Permits — develops policies for compliance, enforcement, and NPDES permits; (b) Office of Water Regulations and Standards — develops effluent guidelines, water quality standards, and monitors national water-related activities; (c) Office of Municipal Pollution Control — develops national strategies and evaluates municipal point source control programs; (d) Office of Drinking Water — develops regulations/guidance to protect drinking water quality and underground sources; (e) Office of Ground-Water Protection — oversees ground-water protection strategy and decision-making framework; (f) Office of Marine and Estuarine Protection — develops policies for marine/estuarine protection including ocean dumping; (g) Office of Wetlands Protection — administers the 404/Wetlands Program and develops policies for wetlands protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional Administrators responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Regional Administrators are responsible to the Administrator, within their Regions, for execution of Regional Programs and serve as the Administrator's principal representatives in contacts and relationships with Federal, State, interstate and local agencies, industry, academic institutions, and other groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Responsibilities include: (a) accomplishing national program objectives within Regions; (b) developing, proposing, and implementing Regional programs for integrated environmental protection activities; (c) total resource management within Headquarters guidelines; (d) conducting effective Regional enforcement and compliance programs; (e) translating technical program direction into effective operating programs at the Regional level; (f) exercising approval authority for proposed State standards and implementation plans; and (g) providing overall and specific evaluations of Regional programs, both internal Agency and State activities.
